davao flooding and the dutertes a balanced assessment an honest starting point flooding in davao is a legitimate concern that deserves serious attention some of the criticisms are grounded in real events including a genuine solid-waste crisis that cost lives this year at the same time much of the social-media commentary exaggerates the problem blurs who's actually responsible and paints this as a uniquely duterte-family failure a fair assessment holds both things at once real gaps and a national context that critics conveniently leave out national reality check flood control is a hard problem everywhere in the philippines outdated drainage garbage-choked waterways siltation and urbanization that outpaced 1970s-era infrastructure overwhelm every major city in heavy rain no lgu not manila not cebu not davao has a flood-free rainy season anyone claiming otherwise about any city is selling something davao carries the same systemic pressures as its peers but has put more visible work into the problem than most what has been delivered multiple drainage and flood-control projects since 2022 prioritized in high-risk districts including river rehabilitation on the matina bunawan and davao river systems seven dpwh pumping stations already operating across the city jerome mamay agdao marginal-to-magsaysay ponce roxas ext mabini ext plus two more in laverna with a third proposed city-funded drainage rehabilitation including php 35 million for the csc road drainage and php 40 million for the kabacan creek in ecoland residents in upgraded zones report noticeably faster water recession after heavy downpours compared to before these projects this is anecdotal rather than a published city metric but it's a consistent report worth taking seriously rather than dismissing rodrigo duterte's earlier line-item vetoes of questionable dpwh insertions reflected a genuine stance against pork-barrel-style spending which matters when we're talking about whether flood money gets spent honestly these are real verifiable steps not just promises where the record is genuinely weak and needs to be said plainly this is the part critics will hammer so let's not soften it on may 20 2026 a portion of the new carmen sanitary landfill collapsed after days of heavy rain killing at least one person and leaving others missing on top of injuries and displaced families denr suspended the landfill days later cited multiple violations of the ecological solid waste management act and permanently closed the old site in june that is not a maintenance footnote it was a fatal disaster and it happened on this administration's watch pretending otherwise would be dishonest beyond that incident the underlying problems are real and longstanding the landfill was already operating well past design capacity for years before it collapsed waste disposal roughly doubled from 2010 levels by 2025 and this was a known documented problem not a surprise drainage systems in several barangays have not received consistent desilting uncollected and improperly dumped garbage continues to clog canals and drainage inlets citywide and enforcement against illegal dumping and drainage encroachment remains inconsistent the new landfill and expansion projects were already underway before the collapse which shows the problem was recognized but recognizing a problem is not the same as having fixed it in time full transparency on the landfill collapse investigation and a public accounting of why the old site was allowed to run so far past capacity is the least residents deserve comparative perspective none of this erases the comparison that matters how does davao stack up against lgus facing the same pressures on project delivery and the resources actually put toward flood mitigation pumping stations river rehabilitation drainage funding davao has more to point to than many cities of similar size and budget that doesn't make davao's flooding acceptable it means the uniquely incompetent duterte fiefdom narrative pushed on social media doesn't survive contact with what other lgus are or aren't doing with comparable resources key clarifications the php 51 billion figure widely cited for rep paolo duterte's district 2020-2022 is routinely presented online as if it were all flood-control spending it wasn't dpwh-davao itself has clarified the figure later refined to php 49.8 billion covered the district's entire infrastructure portfolio roads bridges multipurpose buildings and major projects like the davao coastal road and bypass road dpwh's own breakdown puts the text_content: davao the flood capital but perhaps not for the reason you think they say davao is the flood capital of the philippines well if someone insists on giving us that crown perhaps we should wear it proudly-but let's first ask a simple question what exactly is overflowing yes davao experiences floods we have rivers that swell after relentless rain low-lying communities that sometimes bear the brunt of nature sudden downpours that seem to arrive without an appointment and roads that occasionally transform into temporary swimming pools that is a real problem it deserves real solutions-not political theater but if we are going to compare cities perhaps the scoreboard deserves more than a political slogan during the severe southwest monsoon flooding in july 2025 for example the metropolitan manila development authority reported hundreds of flooding incidents across metro manila within a single day so before anyone points a finger at davao perhaps we should remember that flooding is not a problem exclusive to one city water does not check political affiliations before it rises rain does not ask who you voted for before it pours and rivers certainly don't read campaign speeches but here's where i see davao differently because there is another kind of flooding happening here-one that doesn't destroy homes close roads or leave mud behind davao floods with culture walk through this city and you encounter a living mosaic of mindanao indigenous traditions migrant communities different languages cuisines beliefs stories and histories woven together into one constantly evolving urban tapestry ask someone where they came from and you may discover an entire story behind the answer then inevitably there's food because in davao you can start a conversation about almost anything and somehow end up discussing durian this variety is sweeter no that one has better texture you haven't tried the best one yet suddenly what began as a casual conversation has transformed into an international conference on durian no registration fee required but perhaps davao's most remarkable flood is neither water nor culture it is warmth there is a quiet generosity in the character of many dabawenyos that statistics cannot measure you can arrive as a stranger and before long someone may already be telling you where to eat what places to visit which shortcut to take-and most importantly which road to avoid when traffic is terrible that's not just hospitality that's hospitality with a built-in traffic advisory and then there is davao's natural beauty the sea samal mount apo the forests the farms the rivers the mountains the wide spaces that remind you that progress and nature do not always have to be enemies davao is also changing businesses are arriving buildings are rising infrastructure is expanding communities are growing people continue to come-not only because they are looking for jobs but because they are looking for possibilities some arrive carrying résumés others arrive carrying business plans some arrive carrying nothing more than a dream and somewhere along the way many discover something unexpected they don't merely live in davao they become part of it that perhaps is the real story a city should not be judged solely by the problems that rise within it it should also be judged by what its people continue to build despite those problems davao is not perfect we have traffic we have growing pains we have environmental concerns we have infrastructure challenges we have political disagreements and of course we have social-media experts who can apparently repair the entire country using nothing but a smartphone and a facebook account but beneath all the noise is something far more difficult to construct character you can build a highway you can build skyscrapers you can build malls bridges offices and massive developments you can even build a spectacular roundabout that everyone will complain about for months but you cannot manufacture belonging you cannot pour it into concrete you cannot buy it from a catalog it has to grow and davao has grown through people people from different places came here they planted roots they built families they opened businesses they raised children they created communities and little by little their individual stories became part of the larger story of the city for the past 15 years i have had the privilege of traveling around davao for team-building activities retreats seminars workshops and speaking engagements and in those years i have seen something that no flood statistics can capture i have seen people flood others with smiles generosity and warmth so if someone wants to call davao the flood capital of the philippines perhaps we shouldn't be offended maybe we should simply gabu laoag city a project worth php 47,024,704.34 funded under the 2024 general appropriations act gaa has collapsed just months after its reported completion sparking fresh outrage over the alleged flood-control mafia operating in congress photos taken on-site show large concrete revetments cracked dislodged and washed into the river exposing reinforcing steel and leaving the riverbank vulnerable to further erosion the project billboard names ra pahati construction and supply inc as the contractor under the dpwh ilocos norte first district engineering office with a target completion date of october 4 2024 ra pahati construction is reportedly owned by the family of rep jhong ceniza of pantukan davao de oro a name that has repeatedly surfaced in infrastructure procurement circles sources familiar with congressional contracting allege that ra pahati has become a favored builder for rep sandro marcos the ilocos norte 1st district representative allegedly with some help from his chief of staff said to be a relative of rep ceniza's wife residents and local engineers have raised alarm over the collapse noting that the structure failed despite relatively moderate river flow in recent weeks infrastructure experts point out that proper soil compaction adequate riprap foundation and correct steel reinforcement are crucial in river dike construction all of which appear deficient in the broken sections the collapse has revived long-circulating allegations about flood control allocations being used as a cash cow for certain districts ra pahati controlled by the ceniza family has reportedly bagged billions in contracts across luzon and mindanao despite originating from davao de oro in ilocos norte whispers persist that rep sandro marcos chief of staff reportedly related by marriage to the cenizas has been instrumental in channeling projects to ra pahati bypassing stricter vetting political analysts warn this could become a serious governance issue for the presidential son especially as calls mount for greater transparency in the use of massive dpwh flood control budgets the incident adds to the growing backlash against multi-billion flood control projects nationwide long suspected to be overpriced poorly built and politically manipulated in congress several lawmakers particularly from mindanao have been calling out selective investigations that spare politically allied districts while targeting rivals observers warn that this laoag project could become a flashpoint especially since it sits in the home turf of the president's son who is text_content: when the waters rise in davao city so do the online critics following the heavy rains brought by the habagat and recent weather systems on july 24 2026 several neighborhoods across davao city once again faced rising floodwaters from mandug and tugbok down to low-lying areas like bangkal matina and talomo families had to endure another stressful night of monitoring river levels moving to higher ground or waiting for emergency teams and like clockwork as soon as photos of flooded streets flooded social media the comments section lit up with the usual outrage political potshots and online bashing where did the billions go why hasn't the city solved flooding yet it is completely understandable for affected residents to feel frustrated when water enters their homes but using these calamities to mock or tear down the city overlooks the actual science geography and non-stop work happening on the ground here is the perspective every dabawenyo and onlooker needs to hear 1 you cannot out-engineer a catch basin no politician regardless of their party and no amount of infrastructure spending can change basic topography davao city sits beside major river systems davao talomo matina lipadas bunawan and lasang flowing straight into the gulf key areas like bago gallera talomo proper ulas bangkal and matina are natural catch basins when continuous rains hit the highlands upstream millions of gallons of water naturally rush downward into these lower elevations add a high tide at the coast and the ocean acts like a giant dam preventing river mouths from discharging into the sea dikes and pumping stations can help manage overflow but they cannot stop gravity or push back the ocean 2 nature remembers its original shape parts of boulevard bucana agdao and sta ana were historically mudflats swamps and coastal wetlands humans can pave over these landscapes with roads subdivisions and concrete structures but when extreme rainfall happens water simply reclaims its natural pathways with climate change intensifying weather patterns nationwide rainfall volumes that used to happen once every few decades are now occurring multiple times a year this is a regional and global environmental challenge not an isolated municipal flaw 3 where did the funds go look at the defense systems in place critics often point to multi-billion flood control budgets as if money should make water instantly disappear but flood mitigation infrastructure isn't meant to stop rain from falling it's built to slow down water protect riverbanks and buy critical time pumping stations and retarding basins built in notorious bottlenecks like sasa and la verna to hold runoff and force water past high-tide barriers revetment walls and dikes miles of concrete dikes line the matina talomo and davao rivers to keep riverbanks from completely collapsing during sudden surges early warning and river monitoring the city disaster risk reduction and management office cdrrmo operates automated sensors and live hd monitoring cameras along all six major river channels allowing them to issue preemptive siren alarms and evacuation orders hours before water peaks 4 while keyboard warriors bash responders are out in the dark while critics type away in dry rooms hundreds of frontline responders from the cdrrmo bfp davao light urban search and rescue sar units and barangay disaster teams are out in waist-deep water executing rescue operations clearing clogged channels and moving stranded families to safety good governance in a coastal river-dense city isn't measured by the complete absence of natural calamities it's measured by preparedness quick response and zero casualties the fact that emergency teams can track upstream river swells in real-time and mobilize rescue trucks within minutes is proof of a functional disaster system bashing davao city during a flood won't lower the tide and weaponizing human suffering for online arguments won't stop the rain instead of tearing each other down let's focus on what actually keeps us safe community preparedness and cooperation when the cdrrmo issues a code red or sounds the warning siren do not wait follow evacuation protocols early look out for elderly neighbors keep your emergency kits ready and respect the responders risking their safety on the frontlines davao city has faced heavy weather before and we will always stand resilient through it stay safe stay vigilant and stay proud of our city daghang salamat sa atong responders

text_content: look davao's la verna flood control basin site c to hold almost 11 olympic pools of rainwater construction is moving forward at site c of the three retarding basins rising along la verna creek in buhangin part of the php 211 million flood control project of the department of public works and highways dpwh davao city 3rd district engineering office aerial footage taken on october 9 2026 shows excavators shaping the basin floor beside the existing la verna pumping station along the davao city diversion road cp garcia highway with boulders and steel sheet piles staged on site for the next phase of works once completed site c is designed to hold up to 27,260 cubic meters of stormwater or about 962,679 cubic feet that is almost 11 olympic-size swimming pools worth of capacity from this site alone when all three sites are completed sites a b and c will store a combined 79,460 cubic meters roughly equivalent to 32 olympic-size swimming pools the basins will work hand in hand with the pumping station built in 2019 temporarily holding runoff during heavy rains and releasing it gradually toward the caap outfall the goal is to end the street flooding that has long disrupted traffic in the la verna area keeping one of davao's busiest corridors safe and passable for thousands of daily commuters metro davao rising crown jewel of mindanao davao city danny betonio raneses

higher dike built along talomo river in davao city a higher dike has been completed along a portion of the talomo river in davao city with the project finished within just two months after public works secretary vince dizon ordered the immediate resumption and elevation of the river control structure the project was originally started in 2019 to help prevent severe flooding in communities located near the river the move followed president ferdinand marcos jr s directive to raise the structure by two meters on both sides of the river to help address flooding in the area the planned elevation of the dike was reportedly not pursued at the time allowing the river to overflow and affect nearby homes department of public works and highways

signal no 1 up in parts of northern luzon due to rosal by cristina arayata manila wind signal no 1 has been hoisted in parts of northern luzon as super typhoon rosal international name champi entered the philippine area of responsibility par at around 10:40 a m tuesday areas under signal no 1 are batanes eastern portion of babuyan islands babuyan is camiguin is didicas is eastern portion of mainland cagayan santa ana gonzaga lal-lo santa teresita camalaniugan aparri buguey gattaran baggao peñablanca northeastern portion of isabela maconacon divilacan palanan san pablo cabagan santa maria tumauini ilagan city and northeastern portion of catanduanes pandan bagamanoc panganiban viga gigmoto it doesn't mean that these areas will immediately feel the effects of the wind signal there are at least 36 hours for the people in these areas to prepare for the strong winds philippine atmospheric geophysical and astronomical services administration pagasa forecaster chris perez said in a press conference the cyclone was located 1,385 kilometers east of central luzon outside of par as of 10 a m it is moving west northwestward at 25 kilometers per hour kph rosal packs maximum sustained winds of 185 kph near the center and gustiness of up to 230 kph it is not directly affecting any part of the country the cyclone is forecast to move towards extreme northern luzon taiwan area in the coming days perez said he said no significant rainfall is expected in the next 24 hours perez however said that in the coming days the wind signal may be raised to no 2 or 3 as rosal moves closer to northern luzon as of tuesday pagasa said the northeasterly windflow and rosal's periphery will cause strong to gale-force gusts across batanes ilocos norte cagayan isabela polillo islands camarines norte camarines sur catanduanes northern samar eastern samar most of caraga camiguin misamis oriental sarangani davao del sur and davao occidental meanwhile the cyclone is forecast to weaken into a typhoon on thursday it is expected to exit par on saturday perez added disaster response meanwhile the office of civil defense ocd called on all authorities and the public to take the necessary measures to limit the impact of rosal in an advisory late monday the ocd urged regional and local disaster risk reduction and management councils to strengthen monitoring review contingency plans preposition response resources and ensure the readiness of personnel equipment evacuation centers and critical facilities it also urged closer monitoring of rainfall river and reservoir levels tides low-lying and landslide-prone areas coordinate early warnings and possible preemptive evacuations and prioritize vulnerable groups including persons with disabilities senior citizens and children the public is advised to monitor official weather bulletins and local government advisories prepare emergency supplies secure essential documents and be ready to evacuate when instructed communities are reminded that the ongoing el niño conditions do not eliminate the risks of sudden heavy rainfall flash floods landslides and other hazards it said thus the need for timely coordinated action and sustained public vigilance to protect lives and minimize the potential impacts of the weather disturbance the philippine national police has also alerted its field units and ordered the activation of disaster davao's flood map explained why different neighborhoods face different flood risks when heavy rains hit davao city why do some neighborhoods experience sudden flash floods that recede in a few hours while others remain submerged under standing water for days it all comes down to catchment hydrology the master plan developed by the department of public works and highways dpwh and the japan international cooperation agency jica covers 2,200 square kilometers divided into three main river basins because each catchment has a unique shape slope and size each one poses a completely different flood threat to specific davao neighborhoods 1 davao river basin 1,755 km2 massive volume and standing water neighborhoods affected waan tigatto ma-a barangay 19 barangay 8 and bucana what happens here this is the largest river system in the area because its catchment extends deep into the northern mountain ranges it collects enormous volumes of rainwater even when it isn't raining in the downtown area heavy rainfall up in the mountains eventually travels downstream into the city the engineering reality because the basin is so large there is a time delay before the main wave of water reaches the city as the river passes through tight natural bends near tigatto and ma-a the channel gets squeezed forcing water over the banks worse when peak river flows meet high tides at the river mouth in bucana the seawater acts like a natural dam this creates a severe backwater effect that traps floodwaters inland causing deep slow-draining pools that cover over 480 hectares and affect 43,000 residents 2 matina river basin 70 km2 rapid flash floods and highway bottlenecks neighborhoods affected matina pangi gravahan gsis subdivision and matina crossing what happens here unlike the davao river matina suffers from sudden high-speed flash floods with very little warning time the engineering reality this basin is relatively small steep and heavily built-up with concrete and asphalt because rainwater cannot soak into the ground it immediately rushes straight into the river channel narrow bridge openings-such as the crossing along mcarthur highway-act like narrow bottlenecks when high-volume runoff reaches these tight spots the water backs up rapidly and spills sideways over the banks directly into nearby residential subdivisions 3 talomo river basin 204 km2 raging currents and riverbank collapse neighborhoods affected talomo proper tugbok and communities along the talomo riverbanks what happens here while talomo does not usually create broad standing lakes like the davao river its waters move at extremely high speeds as they surge down from the slopes of mount apo the engineering reality the steep drop in elevation gives the rushing water tremendous kinetic energy instead of long-term standing pools the main danger here is high-velocity water scraping against the riverbed and riverbanks this severe erosion tears away the surrounding land threatens bridge piers and causes steep riverbanks to collapse along the talomo-tugbok corridor 4 the missing gaps intermediate basins and urban creeks neighborhoods affected toril lipadas river bunawan and lasang bunawan/licanan rivers and agdao bajada and buhangin urban creek networks the planning limitation on master plan maps you might notice uncolored spaces between the three big basins in nature land is continuous-every square meter belongs to a catchment the jica study intentionally focused its scope on the three largest high-volume river mains omitting these smaller intermediate catchments why they still matter these smaller watersheds carry severe flood risk for instance the lipadas river in toril causes rapid flash evacuations the bunawan river frequently submerges portions of the davao-agusan highway and dense urban creek networks in agdao and buhangin overflow quickly during short thunderstorms because over 95 percent of the city's natural urban wetlands have been paved over comprehensive city drainage requires addressing these omitted gaps alongside the main rivers the takeaway whether it's standing water along the davao river flash flooding in matina riverbank erosion in talomo or creek overflow in agdao and toril any effective flood strategy must treat all catchments as interconnected systems davao flood control series 4 part deep dive read the full overview post here part 1 text_content: barangay sent 3 warning letters before callawa bridge 2 collapse pacc says davao city the presidential anti-corruption commission pacc has launched a formal investigation into the collapse of callawa bridge 2 after learning that the barangay council of callawa had allegedly sent at least three warning letters to the department of public works and highways dpwh before the structure gave way last week according to the pacc the letters raised serious concerns over visible cracks on the bridge severe erosion beneath the structure exposed bridge foundations and posts and the possibility that the bridge could collapse during heavy flooding residents and barangay officials claimed the warnings were repeatedly brought to the attention of authorities but were allegedly never properly acted upon the bridge collapsed on may 18 following continuous heavy rains triggered by the intertropical convergence zone itcz and easterlies disrupting transportation access and affecting residents and motorists in barangay callawa and nearby communities during an ocular inspection conducted friday pacc officials and volunteer engineers observed extensive erosion and scouring along the bridge approaches with large portions of supporting soil already washed away by strong floodwaters pacc chairman dr louie f ceniza said the incident raises serious concerns about accountability and public safety if prior warnings were indeed raised by the barangay council and residents these concerns should have been immediately addressed before the situation escalated into a disaster ceniza said the people deserve answers the public deserves accountability he added the inspection was conducted in the presence of pacc bot member rev richie cubos dpwh davao city 3rd district engineering office assistant district engineer andrew pangan and volunteer civil engineers from davao city assisting in the initial technical assessment the collapsed structure forms part of the dpwh region xi infrastructure project identified as project id no 17l00133 covering the concreting widening and improvement of the buhangin-tigatto-mandug-callawa-fatima road including reconstruction of callawa bridge the project implemented by dpwh region xi and undertaken by contractor premium megastructures inc cost p190.7 million and was completed in december 2018 initial observations by the pacc indicated that the bridge may have lacked sufficient upstream and downstream flood protection measures investigators said approximately 100 meters of flood control protection on both sides of the bridge could have minimized or prevented the erosion that undermined the structure the pacc also noted the collapse of nearby utility poles due to severe soil erosion and loss of support as part of the probe the commission said it will review approved engineering plans hydraulic and geotechnical studies construction quality control reports inspection and acceptance records maintenance documents and all correspondence submitted by barangay callawa including dpwh responses to the reported concerns pacc bot member and spiritual adviser bishop rod cubos said the incident highlights the consequences of negligence and inaction this incident reminds us that negligence and indifference can lead to suffering danger and hardship within our communities cubos said the pacc emphasized that findings from the inspection remain subject to further technical validation and documentary review meanwhile the commission acknowledged the ongoing efforts of the dpwh davao city 3rd district engineering office headed by ade engr andrew pangan which is currently supervising the construction of a temporary bridge to restore access for affected communities we we

the hostage blueprint jica masterplan for davao city what if i told you that a blueprint to stop the flooding in davao city is already finished it was designed by some of the best engineers in the world printed and is currently sitting on a desk in manila here is the truth about the jica master plan the political war currently holding it hostage and what our local government unit lgu is doing to keep our heads above water while we wait the real solution the jica master plan back in 2018 the philippine government partnered with the japan international cooperation agency jica to solve our city's flooding instead of just building basic concrete walls which easily overflow the japanese and local engineers designed a massive city-wide system the core of the plan involves digging massive retarding basins giant empty catch-ponds built in the uplands when a storm hits millions of gallons of water would flow into these basins and be held there safely trapping the water before it ever reaches barangays like ma-a matina and talomo it is brilliant it is proven and it is ready but just look at the timeline of how it got stuck in politics here is the timeline april 2019 the study begins the philippine government and the japan international cooperation agency jica sign an agreement to create a long-term multi-basin master plan 2018-2022 why wasn't it built under duterte a common question is why this wasn't funded during former president rodrigo duterte's term the answer is engineering reality the japanese engineers were still studying our rivers you cannot fund or construct a mega-project when the architects haven't finished the blueprints july 2023 the blueprint is finished jica officially completes the master plan instead of basic walls it proposes php 41.7 billion to build massive retarding basins giant empty bowls upstream to catch and hold storm water before it hits our urban barangays august 9 2024 vp sara calls out the missing budget vice president sara duterte issues a strong public statement pointing out the lack of government action she calls out the current administration for refusing to fund the finalized master plan questioning if the meet the surigao del sur meteorologist who's now with dost-pagasa blaise christian perez 24 from tandag city surigao del sur is the first graduate of a bachelor of science in meteorology in the province turning his dream into reality the surigaonon meteorologist studied at bicol university and graduated in 2025 he now works in the central office of dost-pagasa blaise shared with ato ni bai that it took him multiple routes before landing in bs meteorology bs meteorology wasn't the most conventional choice and i was very aware of that when i decided to pursue it he said he applied to several universities including adamson university and university of southeastern philippines for a different course but could not pursue it due to the pandemic he enrolled in bs medical laboratory sciences at san pedro college in davao but it didn't work for him blaise admitted that he wasn't fulfilled and struggled to stay motivated he applied again to another school but it did not work out despite these setbacks he never lost sight of his childhood dream and chose to pursue it from a young age he was fascinated by how weather worked drawing inspiration from educational channels and science books especially about natural disasters his grandmother's encouragement of his interest in science nurtured this curiosity which later guided him back to his original dream despite exploring other paths there was this persistent feeling an instinct i couldn't ignore that i should go back to what i originally wanted so i applied for bs meteorology at bicol university which had always been my first choice he recalled according to blaise meteorology was not just a chosen course it was his return to something that had always been part of him what began as a child's quiet curiosity about rain became a lifelong pursuit of understanding the atmosphere and more importantly using that understanding to serve and protect communities he said now the tandaganon meteorologist is working under the hydrometeorology division at the central office of dost-pagasa i'm working as a project technical specialist under ai4rp at dost-pagasa primarily as a researcher within the agency so far the experience has been really fulfilling he shared from what once started as curiosity i now get to work on projects that combine meteorology research and even emerging technologies like ai for disaster risk reduction beyond his research he was able to apply his expertise directly to help his community understand and respond to extreme weather events he proudly shared that he was given an opportunity to speak about the weather in the local language during coordination meetings with the tandag cdrrmo for bagyong tino and basyang these opportunities reinforced his commitment to giving back to his home province he feels a strong desire to contribute and work back in surigao del sur bringing what he has learned to help empower communities i really see the need to strengthen our local drrm efforts especially in terms of climate resilience and more importantly effective science communication sa atong early warning systems kitang tanan naka-experience kung unsa ka grabe ang epekto sa mga bagyo especially recently with ts basyang nga nagdala og grabe nga pagbaha sa atoang probinsya labi na sa tandag he said he also highlights that education and awareness are crucial and preparedness should be prioritized especially in the community people should be well-informed of pagasa forecasts including warnings and know what to do before during and after a hazard hindi man natin mapipigilan ang bagyo o ulan but through preparedness we can save lives ma minusan ang damage and make our communities more resilient he added to those planning to pursue meteorology blaise shared that they should build a strong foundation in math and physics he advised them to stay curious and explore be patient with themselves and remember that the field is not just about forecasting it is about serving people and communities padayon lang gyud even if the path feels uncertain or uncommon dili man siya popular nga course but that doesn't make it any less important if anything mas kinahanglan pa gani siya karon he shared from a curious child in tandag city to a meteorologist with plans for his home province's disaster preparedness blaise shows how passion persistence and dedication can
